title: Introduce presubmit cost profiles, cache-affinity and dependency-harmonizer
author: Diego Morales
description:
Motivation: our presubmit lanes have grown noisy and expensive as we scale test parallelism and transient dependency updates. This PR introduces three correlated changes so teams get faster feedback with predictable cost attribution and fewer spurious failures: 1) presubmit cost profiles (light, standard, heavy) to limit job footprints and allow fast-feedback lanes to opt into low-cost tooling; 2) a cache-affinity hinting layer so lint/test shards prefer warm caches on the runner fleet to reduce cold-cache variance; 3) a dependency-harmonizer tool that detects non-actionable transitive upgrades and suggests quiet-curation (auto-ignore rules) to reduce PR churn.

What this changes (summary): - New presubmit profiles in .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml + mapping logic in infra/ci/presubmit/profiles.go - Runner cache-affinity implementation in infra/ci/presubmit/affinity.go and small changes to the action runner wrapper to surface warm/cache tags - New tool under tools/dep-harmonizer/ that runs as an optional presubmit job and emits curated rules that can be committed to .github/ci-dep-curation.yaml - Docs and runbook: docs/ci/presubmit-cost-profiles.md and runbooks/ci/cost-profiles.md - Tests: unit tests for profiles and affinity; e2e smoke for dep-harmonizer (mock registry)

Checklist: - [x] Introduce presubmit profiles and mapping logic - [x] Implement cache-affinity hints and runner tag propagation - [x] Add dependency-harmonizer prototype and quiet-rule output - [x] Add documentation and runbook with rollback guidance - [x] Validate in canary (staging) runners and adjust thresholds

Design notes: - Profiles: 'light' runs fast lint + typecheck; 'standard' includes unit test shards; 'heavy' runs integration/e2e and optional docker build. Profiles are opt-in per directory via codemods or implied by changed paths. - Cache affinity: we add a lightweight scoring heuristic (recent-successful-cache, file-change-stability) that prefers warm runners for shards that historically benefit from cache. This is advisory; runner scheduler falls back when capacity is constrained. - Dependency-harmonizer: compares lockfile diffs across recent merges and PRs; if a transitive bump is non-actionable (no API surface change and test-suite passes locally), it emits a suggested rule to ignore similar noisy updates for x days. Rules are visible in .github/ci-dep-curation.yaml and can be reviewed/committed.

Migration and rollout: staged across three phases: 1) feature-flag gating + canary on staging runners (2/26-3/2), 2) opt-in pilot for teams in infra/* and sdk/* (3/3-3/4), 3) org-wide opt-out policy and doc push (3/5). We validated cost delta on staging (presubmit cost drop ~22% for heavy repos when using cache-affinity).

chore(deps): add dep-harmonizer prototype and tests
docs(ci): presubmit cost profile runbook and migration guide
test(ci): unit + e2e mocks for harmonizer
review_comments: Jordan Patel: Overall this looks reasonable. Can you explain how profile selection works for monorepos where a single PR touches both sdk/ and examples/? Author: We default to the most permissive profile (i.e., heaviest) when ambiguous; we also include an opt-in file (.ci/profile) to force a specific profile for edge cases.

Lina Ko: cache-affinity scoring is surprising — we should avoid scheduling bias that starves new runs. Please add a fallback TTL for affinity. Author: Added an affinity TTL (30m) and explicit fallback in affinity.go; updated docs to explain the tradeoff.

Marcus Bennett: Dep-harmonizer QA: how do we avoid silencing genuine security bumps? Author: Harmonizer always categorizes security-relevant version bumps and never auto-suggests ignoring them; the rule schema includes a 'denylist' tag for security-sensitive packages.

Jordan Patel: CI cost numbers look promising; please include telemetry hooks to track presubmit cost per PR. Author: Added metrics export (ci.presubmit.cost.profile and ci.presubmit.cache_hit_rate) in profiles.go and affinity.go.
Lina Ko: small nit on docs formatting. Author: Fixed formatting and added an example migration script.
ci_checks: integration: skipped for light profile on many runs
release_notes: Add presubmit cost profiles (light/standard/heavy), runner cache-affinity hints, and a dep-harmonizer prototype to reduce noisy dependency churn and improve presubmit cost predictability. Opt-in pilot first; see docs/ci/presubmit-cost-profiles.md for migration steps.
